history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: 'Kamadgiri Temple' (CSV row 2373) is the same record as seq 1785 (id kamadgiri-temple) - the Kamta Nath Mandir / Kamadgiri hill complex at Chitrakoot; merge or drop one. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV row lists Chitrakoot, Uttar Pradesh, but the existing record places the Kamta Nath Mandir and parikrama path on the Satna (Madhya Pradesh) side; the hill and its ~5 km parikrama circuit straddle the MP-UP border, so both states claim it. NON-TEMPLE: KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED - Kamadgiri is a sacred HILL (the 5 km parikrama circuit, the 'original Chitrakoot'), not a single temple building; a Kamtanath shrine stands at the northern gate but this record is for the hill/landscape itself, like the seq 2237 sacred-tank precedent. Kamadgiri - 'the mountain that fulfills all desires' - is regarded as the original Chitrakoot, the hill where Lord Rama, Sita and Lakshmana lived during their exile. Legend holds that when Rama performed his father Dasharatha's shraddha here, the gods who attended forgot their departure mantra and stayed on, making the hill their permanent abode. The hill is venerated as the embodiment of Lord Rama himself (Kamtanath, the presiding deity of the whole Chitrakoot region, with Sita as Kamadgiri Devi). A ~5 km circumambulation (parikrama/giri-pradakshina) path encircles the hill, lined with temples including Kamtanath and Bharat Milap; barefoot parikrama is believed to wash away sins and grant wishes.

name: Kamadgiri Temple
town_description: Chitrakoot is an ancient pilgrimage town spread across the Madhya Pradesh-Uttar Pradesh border, sacred in the Ramayana as the place of Lord Rama's 11-plus years of exile. Its key sites - Kamadgiri, Ram Ghat on the Mandakini river, Hanuman Dhara and Gupt Godavari - draw lakhs of pilgrims, especially on Amavasya days. The MP-side town is Chitrakoot (Satna district), connected by road and rail, with an operational domestic airport at nearby Karwi.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism) - sacred landscape (hill/parikrama), not a temple building
